expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official coverage, take-up, customer-service, regulatory, switching, complaint, procurement or programme-management fact

facts.detail: The Spring 2026 update is an interim snapshot of mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
Fixed broadband reporting covers fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access availability and also reports full-fibre take-up.
The update retains the decent-broadband threshold of at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Mobile coverage is reported using signal-strength predictions supplied by the four mobile network operators.

guard_streams.write_limit: A national January snapshot and operator predictions are not exact live parcel serviceability or measured-speed evidence.

facts.detail: Full fibre was reported available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of homes.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections, corresponding to 47% of premises with access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 27.1 million homes, or 89%.
Ofcom reported around 4,000 premises without affordable decent broadband and 39,000 unable to obtain decent broadband from fixed line or fixed wireless access.

guard_streams.write_limit: National totals and percentages cannot be assigned to an individual postcode or parcel without the accepted postcode-level dataset.

facts.detail: Gigabit and full-fibre coverage headline figures focus on residential properties, while full-fibre take-up and decent-broadband gaps cover residential and commercial premises combined.
Lower-priced Starlink plans in selected areas reduced the estimate of premises lacking affordable decent broadband.
Around 7,000 additional commercial premises were not included in the USO eligibility estimate because some may already use connections such as leased lines.
Ofcom provides downloadable supporting data subject to its licence and terms-of-use conditions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Different denominator scopes, selected-area satellite offers and possible leased-line use require fail-closed parcel interpretation.

facts.detail: The current page describes Ofcom's eighth comparative customer-service report for residential telecoms customers.
The report covers customer-service experiences in 2024 and compares them with 2022 and/or 2023.
Ofcom moved from annual to biennial Comparing Customer Service reporting after the 2023 publication.
The report is intended to support informed provider choice and incentivise service-quality improvement.

guard_streams.write_limit: Survey and provider-level customer-service comparisons are not parcel network-performance measurements.

facts.detail: Overall satisfaction across mobile, broadband and landline customers remained high in the 2024 evidence.
Overall satisfaction with complaints handling increased significantly in 2024 compared with 2022.
Call-abandonment rates varied considerably by provider and broadband and landline fault outcomes were mixed.
After an April 2026 EE resubmission, specified EE faults data and associated industry averages remain subject to restatement.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider-level survey findings and data subject to restatement must not change parcel confidence or coverage fields.

facts.detail: The General Conditions apply to providers of electronic communications networks and services operating in the UK.
Ofcom identifies an unofficial consolidated version of the current General Conditions that came into force on 8 April 2026.
General Conditions can apply to all providers or to providers of networks or services of a specified description.
General Conditions differ from universal-service, significant-market-power and access-related conditions that can have different legal bases or targets.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regulatory applicability does not prove current service availability, technology or performance at an address.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom One Touch Switch enforcement programme

facts.detail: Ofcom opened an industry-wide enforcement programme concerning One Touch Switch implementation.
The programme was triggered by industry's failure to implement the required process by 3 April 2023.
The enforcement-programme page was last updated on 11 June 2026.
One Touch Switch compliance concerns customer transfer processes rather than the underlying broadband technology or parcel availability.

guard_streams.write_limit: Enforcement and switching-process status cannot be treated as evidence of parcel coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: The update covers complaints received during October to December 2025.
Overall telecoms complaints increased quarter on quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband and landline complaint rates decreased while pay-TV was unchanged and mobile complaints increased.
TalkTalk and Vodafone were the most complained-about broadband providers, while Plusnet and Virgin Media were the least complained-about.

guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly provider complaint rates are provider-level customer-service evidence and not address-level network measurements.

guard_streams.source: BDUK East Gloucestershire Project Gigabit contract

facts.detail: The East Gloucestershire Project Gigabit contract was awarded to Gigaclear.
The contract value is £16 million for around 4,400 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in February 2024.
Preparatory construction precedes service access and the premise list can change through detailed planning or technical constraints.

guard_streams.write_limit: A procurement award and planned build sequence do not establish present parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Yorkshire and parts of North Yorkshire contract

facts.detail: The West Yorkshire and parts of North Yorkshire contract was awarded to Quickline.
The award is £60 million for around 28,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in February 2024.
Trenching, duct and fibre work are required before access and planned premises remain subject to planning or technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract scope, value and anticipated construction do not prove current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North East Staffordshire Project Gigabit contract

facts.detail: The North East Staffordshire contract was awarded to Connect Fibre.
The award is £16.5 million for around 6,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in November 2023.
The supplier must complete detailed planning before network construction and service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award and planning records cannot be promoted to current address-level coverage or connection status.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North Dorset Project Gigabit contract

facts.detail: The North Dorset contract was awarded to Wessex Internet.
The award is £6 million for more than 7,000 premises.
The contract was signed on 25 August 2022.
Network build precedes connection requests and contract scope is subject to detailed-planning and technical changes.

guard_streams.write_limit: Historical anticipated delivery and contract targeting do not prove current parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Openreach Project Gigabit framework agreement

facts.detail: The framework page records eight awarded Openreach call-off contracts.
Call-off two covers Devon, Mid Wales and South East Wales with a £137.2 million value and 41,140 contracted premises.
Call-off six covers the rest of Scotland with a £175.5 million value and 77,640 contracted premises.
Call-off eight covers Cheshire with a £37.5 million value and 18,460 contracted premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Framework call-off values and contracted counts are programme scope, not present parcel build or orderability evidence.

guard_streams.source: BDUK July 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress

facts.detail: The July management table is a snapshot of BDUK data held on 16 July 2026.
Contract-management figures are not directly comparable with BDUK official statistics because they measure different concepts.
The publication warns of variable lag between contract signature or delivery and ingestion into BDUK systems.
Figures are rounded to the nearest ten and totals may not sum because of rounding.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded contract-level management snapshots cannot determine current exact parcel delivery or milestone compliance.

guard_streams.source: Canonical slot state and exact-output acceptance

facts.detail: Canonical continuation and runtime records show no live owner.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING execution exists.
The legacy heartbeat path remains absent; terminal continuation and runtime records are used as the ownership fallback.
No candidate, measured-speed row or accuracy promotion is allowed before accepted r2 archive bytes, exact join and hardened postjoin readback.

guard_streams.write_limit: The final operation remains blocked until the canonical Windows host produces validated archive and postjoin evidence.

probe_evidence.method: official Ofcom and GOV.UK HTML verification plus canonical continuation/runtime/manual readback
